base: black-and-white editorial vintage documentary photograph, desaturated, high contrast, grainy film texture. WIDE HORIZONTAL LANDSCAPE orientation, 3:2 aspect ratio, much wider than tall. FRAMING IS CRITICAL: the camera is CLOSE and the subject is VERY LARGE, filling the entire BOTTOM THREE QUARTERS of the frame from the left edge to the right edge, extending past the bottom edge. Only a NARROW BAND across the very TOP of the frame, about one fifth of the height, is empty pale bright almost-white wall or light, completely free of objects. EVERYTHING IS IN SHARP CRISP FOCUS, deep depth of field, no blur, no bokeh, no soft focus. This is ONE single real photographic exposure, never a composite: every element shares the same light and grain. THE TOP OF THE FRAME IS BRIGHT OVEREXPOSED LIGHT, and the transition from the scene into that light is GRADUAL and soft, as if the light swallows the upper part of the scene: NO horizontal edge anywhere, no shelf edge, no ceiling line, no sign, no roofline crossing the top. Surfaces and objects fade softly upward into the light. THE TOP BAND IS A HARD REQUIREMENT: that top fifth must be ONE single continuous evenly-lit pale surface spanning the FULL width, bright and uniform, with NOTHING crossing it at all: no shelf, no beam, no lamp, no head, no edge of any object. It must read as smooth blank paper. NO fog, NO mist, NO haze and NO smoke anywhere inside the scene itself; only that narrow band at the very top is pale. Natural unposed body language. Brazil, late 1970s; every sign, card, notebook, photograph, uniform or object in the scene is PLAIN and UNBRANDED: no printed brand names, no logos, no legible writing of any kind; any papers, notebooks, punch cards or photographs show only vague illegible marks, never readable letters or numbers. No text, no words, no letters, no numbers, no logos, no emojis, no gradients, no added color, no stock photo look.
cinema: CINEMATIC DIRECTION: camera at chest height, one strong directional light source raking across the scene, deep shadows, dramatic contrast. People LARGE and CLOSE, chest up, heads at about one fifth from the top of the frame. Every person is FULLY inside the frame: heads complete with clear empty space above them, nobody cropped at the neck, shoulders or waist, nobody touching the left or right edges.
fit: COMPOSITION FOR THE SLIDE (HARD REQUIREMENT): the subject occupies ONLY the LOWER 55 percent of the frame; the ENTIRE UPPER 45 percent of the frame is a plain, flat, evenly lit surface in a very pale OFF-WHITE tone (like unbleached linen paper, hex F3F3F3), with a faint fine texture and absolutely nothing on it: no shelves, no objects, no doorway, no window, no sign, no ceiling line, no heads. That pale surface is part of the photograph and simply continues upward, staying very pale and uniform to the top edge.

images.scene: Inside a beverage distribution warehouse in Brazil, late 1970s: the OWNER, a man in his fifties in a plain short-sleeved shirt, holding a clipboard (blank, illegible), stands FACE TO FACE with a big, burly adult EMPLOYEE in a plain work uniform who has his ARMS CROSSED and his CHIN RAISED, listening without agreeing, jaw set. Both LARGE, chest up, in profile to the camera, heads in the lower half of the frame. Behind them a parked hand pallet truck and stacked crates low in the frame; the bare pale warehouse wall above everything.

Small office of a print shop in Brazil, late 1970s: the OWNER, a man in his fifties, sits at his desk with one HAND RAISED mid-sentence, mouth slightly open, left alone; in the foreground an EMPLOYEE seen from BEHIND is walking OUT through the open door, back turned, already leaving. Both LARGE; the owner chest up, head in the lower half of the frame; the bare pale office wall above.

Behind the counter of a small neighborhood pharmacy in Brazil, late 1970s: the OWNER in a white pharmacist coat leans in and speaks in a LOW voice, shoulders hunched, almost apologetic, hands half open; the female EMPLOYEE in a plain white uniform stands with ARMS CROSSED, looking AWAY from him to the side, unmoved. Both LARGE, chest up, heads in the lower half of the frame; plain pale wall above, no shelves visible above them.

STILL LIFE, close: the small break-room table of a Brazilian company, late 1970s, the morning after a little party: a cut sponge cake with a few slices missing on a plate, several used coffee cups, crumpled paper napkins, and two DEFLATED, wrinkled balloons lying on the table; on the pale wall behind, low in the frame, a plain chalkboard with an empty ruled table (illegible marks only). The table fills the lower part of the frame edge to edge. NO PEOPLE anywhere in the frame, no hands, no faces, no silhouettes.

A Brazilian man in his fifties, the owner, sitting on the EDGE OF HIS BED before dawn in a plain white undershirt, ELBOWS ON HIS KNEES, hands hanging, holding a dark switched-off telephone handset loosely in one hand, staring at the floor, awake and worried; the bedroom dim, a bedside lamp low. He is LARGE, chest up, head in the lower half of the frame; the bare pale bedroom wall above him.

STILL, close: a single BLANK sheet of paper taped with two strips of tape to the plain pale wall of a furniture workshop in Brazil, late 1970s, and a man's HAND and FOREARM entering from the lower right, index finger POINTING firmly at the blank sheet. Only the hand and forearm are visible, no face, no body; the sheet is low in the frame, the wall continues pale above it. Sawdust and a workbench edge at the very bottom.

Inside a small tire repair shop in Brazil, late 1970s: TWO men FACE TO FACE, an owner in a plain shirt and a mechanic in oil-stained overalls, BOTH pointing an index finger at each other at the same time, arguing, jaws tense; a big truck tire standing on the floor between them. Both LARGE, chest up, heads in the lower half of the frame; the bare pale shop wall above them.

STILL: a frosted-glass office door standing AJAR in a small Brazilian company, late 1970s, and through the frosted glass the blurred dark SHADOW of a man standing still on the other side, about to come in; in the foreground, on a desk low in the frame, a half-finished job: an open ledger with illegible marks, a pen dropped mid-line, a cup of coffee. The door and desk fill the lower part of the frame; the pale wall continues above. No visible face, no visible person, only the shadow behind the glass.

Office of a small trucking company in Brazil, late 1970s: the OWNER, a man in his fifties, and a younger EMPLOYEE in a plain shirt sit SIDE BY SIDE on the SAME side of a wooden desk, both leaning over ONE open sheet of paper between them (illegible marks only), the owner POINTING at a line on the sheet with a pen, the employee nodding and looking at the page, calm. Both LARGE, chest up, heads in the lower half of the frame; the bare pale office wall above.

Early morning in a plain meeting room of a small Brazilian company, late 1970s: FIVE people, men and women in plain work clothes, STANDING in a loose half circle around a whiteboard on an easel that shows a simple hand-drawn table (illegible marks only), each holding a small coffee cup, nobody sitting, listening; the owner among them pointing at the board. All LARGE, chest up, heads in the lower half of the frame; the bare pale wall above them and above the board.

STILL, close: on the plain pale wall of a Brazilian factory, late 1970s, a round industrial WALL CLOCK with a plain white face and black hands showing EIGHT o'clock (no numbers, no brand), and directly BELOW it a wooden clipboard hanging from a single nail, holding a blank sheet of paper. Both objects sit LOW in the frame, the clock in the lower half; the pale wall continues empty above them. NO PEOPLE anywhere in the frame, no hands, no faces, no silhouettes.

STILL LIFE, close, from above at an angle: a fountain pen resting on a sheet of paper HANDWRITTEN in ink (illegible marks only) with TWO SIGNATURES at the bottom, on a worn wooden table in Brazil, late 1970s; a coffee ring stain on the wood, a small tin ashtray at the edge. The sheet fills the lower part of the frame; the pale wall or bright tabletop continues plain above. NO PEOPLE anywhere in the frame, no hands, no faces, no silhouettes.

Inside a small upholstery factory in Brazil, late 1970s: the OWNER, a man in his fifties in a plain shirt, stands CALM at the HEAD of a long wooden work table with a clipboard tucked under his arm, watching; along the table four workers sit sewing and stapling fabric onto chair frames, concentrated, the closest one LARGE in the foreground. Heads in the lower half of the frame; the bare pale factory wall above.

STILL, close: a wooden CLIPBOARD hanging from a hook on the plain pale wall of a Brazilian warehouse, late 1970s, holding a sheet with a few illegible handwritten lines, a ballpoint pen TIED to the clipboard with a piece of string dangling; warm late-afternoon light raking across the wall from the side. The clipboard sits low in the frame; the pale wall continues empty above it. NO PEOPLE anywhere in the frame, no hands, no faces, no silhouettes.
